plan.title: Alan Turing: The Mind That Shaped Computing
plan.description: Alan Turing was a British mathematician who helped break wartime codes and laid the foundations of computer science. This video explains his ideas, his work, and why he still matters.

beats.narration: Can a machine think? Long before smartphones, one British mathematician asked that question and gave us a way to explore it. His name was Alan Turing, and his ideas still shape our world.

props.title: Alan Turing
props.subtitle: The mathematician who asked if machines can think

beats.narration: Turing was born in England in the early twentieth century. He was curious and brilliant from a young age, and he loved numbers, puzzles and the logic behind how things work.

In the 1930s he imagined a simple theoretical machine. It read symbols, followed rules and could, in principle, carry out any calculation. This idea, now called the Turing machine, became a foundation of computer science.
Think of it as a blueprint. Every laptop and phone you use today does, at heart, what his imaginary machine described: it follows instructions step by step.
During the Second World War, Turing worked with a team of codebreakers in Britain. Their task was to read secret enemy messages, protected by machines that scrambled every letter.
Turing helped design methods and machines to speed up that work. Many historians believe the codebreakers' success shortened the war and saved a great many lives.

props.text: Codebreaking may have shortened the war and saved many lives.

beats.narration: After the war, Turing kept thinking about intelligence. He proposed a test: if a person chatting with a hidden machine cannot tell it from a human, the machine might be called intelligent.

turns.speaker: Judge
turns.text: Are you a person or a machine?

turns.speaker: Hidden voice
turns.text: Can you tell the difference from my answers?

beats.narration: Today we call it the Turing test. It still sparks debate as artificial intelligence writes, talks and answers questions in ways that once sounded like science fiction.
Yet his life was hard. Britain punished him for being gay, which was then a crime. He died in 1954, and the country later apologized for how it treated him.

props.text: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.

beats.chapter: A hard ending, a lasting legacy

beats.narration: Turing's work gave us the idea of the computer, a method for judging machine intelligence, and a reminder of what prejudice can cost. Remember his name whenever you pick up a device.
